ops.title: Run entries with shell operators rejected as unrecognized to prevent injection
ops.body: contract.py's `is_attach_argv`/`is_canonical_run_argv` (shared by pack lint AND scaffold) tighten to the exact generated grammar and reject any command carrying a shell control operator/redirection/substitution char (`carries_shell_operator`, `SHELL_METACHARS = frozenset(";&|<>()` + backtick + newlines)). A token like `run Stop && /opt/audit` or the glued `run Stop&&/opt/audit` no longer classifies as canonical-run: scaffold would have *stripped* that entry (deleting the foreign command); lint would have accepted it as a bare "run entry". Both now classify it as "unrecognized" — lint FAILS it, scaffold REFUSES (never rewrites). Design choice: DETECT-AND-REJECT the whole entry as invalid input, never parse/sanitize the operators out. The length check alone is insufficient (glued `Stop&&/x` is one shlex token), so the metachar scan is load-bearing. `$` `{` `}` `/` `-` are deliberately NOT metachars (needed by `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and event/flag tokens); `$(` is caught via `(`. Fixed in capt-hook commit e17adb5e (review-fix wave).
